questions.source: NCERT Exemplar Class 11 Ch 3 Q3.1 / NEET PYQ
questions.question: A vehicle travels half the total distance L with speed v1 and the remaining half with speed v2. Its average speed over the entire journey is:

options.trap: Trap: Arithmetic mean applies ONLY when time intervals are equal, NOT distance intervals!
Correct: Harmonic mean for equal distances.
Trap: Geometric mean has no physical basis here.
Trap: Missing factor of 2 in numerator.

questions.trap_warning: Confusing average speed over equal distance vs. equal time intervals.
questions.explanation: Total distance = L. Time for first half = (L/2)/v1. Time for second half = (L/2)/v2. Total time = L/2 * (1/v1 + 1/v2) = L(v1+v2)/(2 v1 v2). Average speed = Total Distance / Total Time = 2 v1 v2 / (v1 + v2).

questions.source: NCERT Exemplar Class 11 Ch 4 Q4.1 / NEET PYQ
questions.question: Two vectors A and B have equal magnitudes |A| = |B| = R. If the magnitude of their resultant |A + B| is also equal to R, what is the angle θ between the two vectors?

options.trap: Trap: Confused with angle when |A - B| = R.
Trap: At 90°, resultant is R√2.
Correct: 2R² + 2R² cosθ = R² => cosθ = -1/2 => θ = 120°.
Trap: At 180°, resultant is zero.

questions.trap_warning: Forgetting that vector addition involves 2AB cosθ. For |A+B|=R, cosθ must be -0.5 (obtuse angle).
questions.explanation: |A + B|² = A² + B² + 2AB cosθ. Since A = B = R: R² = R² + R² + 2R² cosθ => R² = 2R²(1 + cosθ) => 1 + cosθ = 1/2 => cosθ = -1/2 => θ = 120°.

questions.question: A projectile is launched with velocity v₀ = 50 m/s at an angle of 30° with the VERTICAL. What is the maximum vertical height reached? (Take g = 10 m/s²)

options.trap: Trap: Blindly applied sin²(30°) from textbook horizontal formula!
Correct: Uses cos²(30°) = 0.75 for vertical velocity component.
Trap: Assumed pure vertical launch (90°).
Trap: Arithmetic error in squaring velocity.

questions.trap_warning: Swapping sine and cosine: angle is relative to VERTICAL axis, so vertical velocity is v₀ cos θ.
questions.explanation: Because the angle is specified relative to the vertical axis, the upward vertical velocity component is vy = v₀ cos(30°) = 50 · (√3/2) = 25√3 m/s. H_max = vy² / (2g) = (25√3)² / (2 · 10) = (625 · 3) / 20 = 1875 / 20 = 93.75 m.

questions.source: NCERT Exemplar Class 11 Ch 4 Q4.7 / NEET PYQ
questions.question: A particle moves in a circle of radius r with constant angular velocity ω. What is the work done by the centripetal force on the particle during one complete revolution?

options.text: A) 2π r · mω²r
options.trap: Trap: Multiplied force by circumference, ignoring direction!

options.text: B) Zero
options.trap: Correct: Centripetal force is always perpendicular to instantaneous displacement (F ⊥ dr => W = 0).

options.text: C) mω²r²
options.trap: Trap: Equated work to kinetic energy.

options.text: D) (1/2) mω²r²
options.trap: Trap: Equated work to rotational energy.

questions.trap_warning: Centripetal force does ZERO work at every instant because angle between force and velocity is 90°.
questions.explanation: Work done dW = F · dr = F · v dt = F v cos(90°) dt = 0. Centripetal force changes only the direction of velocity, not the kinetic energy.

questions.question: A physical quantity X is given by X = (A² · B³) / (C · √D). If the percentage errors in A, B, C, and D are 1%, 2%, 3%, and 4% respectively, what is the maximum percentage error in X?

options.trap: Trap: Subtracted denominator errors instead of adding maximum fractional errors!
Trap: Subtracted errors of C and D.
Trap: Missed exponent of B.

questions.trap_warning: Errors always add up in worst-case analysis; NEVER subtract errors in denominators!

questions.source: NCERT Exemplar Class 11 Ch 5 Q5.4 / NEET PYQ
questions.question: A block of mass m rests on a rough horizontal surface with coefficient of static friction μs. A horizontal force F is applied, but the block remains at rest. What is the magnitude of the frictional force acting on the block?

options.text: A) μs · m g
options.trap: Trap: μs·mg is the LIMITING maximum friction, not actual friction before slipping!

options.text: B) F
options.trap: Correct: Static friction is self-adjusting and exactly equals applied force F until motion starts.

options.text: C) Zero
options.trap: Trap: Friction exists to oppose the tendency of relative motion.

options.text: D) m g / μs
options.trap: Trap: Dimensionally incorrect.

questions.trap_warning: Static friction is self-adjusting (fs = F applied). It only equals μs·N when on the verge of impending motion!
questions.explanation: As long as the block remains at rest, equilibrium requires Σ Fx = 0 => F - fs = 0 => fs = F. Only when F exceeds the limiting threshold μs·mg does the block slip.

questions.question: If the linear momentum of a body is increased by 50%, what is the percentage increase in its kinetic energy?

options.trap: Trap: Assumed kinetic energy is linearly proportional to momentum.
Trap: Rough estimate error.
Correct: K = p²/(2m). If p' = 1.5p, K' = (1.5)² K = 2.25 K => increase = 125%.
Trap: 225% is the final kinetic energy, the INCREASE is 225 - 100 = 125%!

questions.trap_warning: Differentiating between 'final value' (225%) and 'percentage increase' (125%)!
questions.explanation: K = p² / (2m). New momentum p' = p + 0.5p = 1.5p. New KE K' = (1.5p)² / (2m) = 2.25 K. Percentage increase = ((K' - K)/K) * 100 = (2.25 - 1) * 100 = 125%.

questions.chapter_name: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.question: A solid cylinder and a hollow cylinder of the same mass M and same radius R roll down an inclined plane without slipping starting from rest. Which one reaches the bottom first?

options.text: A) Solid cylinder
options.trap: Correct: Solid cylinder has smaller moment of inertia (I = 1/2 MR² vs MR²), hence larger linear acceleration a = g sinθ / (1 + I/MR²).

options.text: B) Hollow cylinder
options.trap: Trap: Hollow cylinder has larger rotational inertia, which retards linear acceleration.

options.text: C) Both reach simultaneously
options.trap: Trap: True only in frictionless sliding, not in rolling!

options.text: D) Depends on inclination angle θ
options.trap: Trap: Acceleration ratio is independent of θ.

questions.trap_warning: In pure rolling on an incline, a = g sinθ / (1 + k²/R²). Smaller k²/R² means faster descent.
questions.explanation: For solid cylinder k²/R² = 1/2 = 0.5. For hollow cylinder k²/R² = 1.0. Acceleration a_solid = (2/3) g sinθ > a_hollow = (1/2) g sinθ. Therefore, the solid cylinder accelerates faster and reaches the bottom first.

questions.question: The escape velocity from the Earth is ve = 11.2 km/s. If a body is projected at an angle of 45° to the horizontal, what is its escape velocity?

options.trap: Trap: Assumed escape velocity depends on launch angle!

options.text: B) 11.2 km/s
options.trap: Correct: Escape velocity ve = √(2GM/R) is a scalar and completely independent of projection angle.
Trap: Component miscalculation.

options.text: D) Zero
options.trap: Trap: Nonsensical distractor.

questions.trap_warning: Escape velocity is a pure energy condition (E_total >= 0). Direction of launch does NOT change ve!
questions.explanation: Escape condition requires Total Energy = (1/2) m ve² - GMm/R >= 0 => ve = √(2GM/R). Since kinetic energy is scalar, escape velocity depends only on mass and radius of the planet, entirely independent of the projection angle.

questions.question: Two soap bubbles of radii r1 and r2 (with r1 > r2) are connected by a tube with a closed stopcock. When the stopcock is opened, what happens?

options.text: A) Air flows from the smaller bubble to the larger bubble, making the smaller one smaller.
options.trap: Correct: Excess pressure is ΔP = 4T/r. Smaller radius r2 means higher internal pressure!

options.text: B) Air flows from the larger bubble to the smaller bubble until both radii are equal.
options.trap: Trap: Intuitive common sense assumption, which is opposite to Young-Laplace physics!

options.text: C) No air flows because both are made of the same soap solution.
options.trap: Trap: Ignores radius dependence of Laplace pressure.

options.text: D) Both bubbles immediately burst.
options.trap: Trap: Distractor.

questions.trap_warning: Counter-intuitive NEET trap: Inside pressure is inversely proportional to radius (P ∝ 1/r). Smaller bubbles have HIGHER pressure!
questions.explanation: Excess pressure inside a soap bubble is ΔP = 4T/r. Since r2 < r1, the pressure inside the smaller bubble is strictly greater than inside the larger bubble (P2 > P1). Air flows from high pressure to low pressure, so the small bubble shrinks into the large one.

questions.question: A Carnot engine operates between source temperature T1 = 500 K and sink temperature T2 = 300 K. If it absorbs 1000 J of heat from the source per cycle, the work done per cycle is:

options.trap: Trap: 600 J is heat rejected to the sink Q2 = 1000 * (300/500), not the work done!
Correct: Efficiency η = 1 - T2/T1 = 1 - 300/500 = 0.4. Work W = η · Q1 = 0.4 · 1000 = 400 J.
Trap: Violates Second Law of Thermodynamics (100% efficiency impossible).
Trap: Calculation error.

questions.trap_warning: Make sure whether question asks for 'Work done' (W = η Q1) or 'Heat rejected' (Q2 = (1-η) Q1).
questions.explanation: Efficiency η = 1 - (T2/T1) = 1 - (300/500) = 0.4. Work done W = η · Q1 = 0.4 · 1000 J = 400 J. Heat rejected Q2 = Q1 - W = 600 J.

questions.question: In a simple harmonic motion with amplitude A, at what displacement x from the mean position is the kinetic energy equal to the potential energy?

options.text: A) x = A / 2
options.trap: Trap: At x = A/2, PE is (1/4) of total energy, while KE is (3/4) of total energy!
Correct: PE = (1/2) k x² = (1/2) Total Energy => x² = A²/2 => x = A/√2.

options.text: C) x = A / 4
options.trap: Trap: Distractor.
Trap: Distractor.

questions.trap_warning: Energy depends on x SQUARED (x²). Half the total energy occurs at x = A/√2 ≈ 0.707 A, NOT at A/2!
questions.explanation: Total Energy E = (1/2) k A². When KE = PE, PE = (1/2) E => (1/2) k x² = (1/2) [ (1/2) k A² ] => x² = A²/2 => x = A / √2.

questions.source: NEET PYQ 2023 / NCERT Exemplar Class 12 Ch 1
questions.question: A parallel plate capacitor is connected to a battery of voltage V. While the battery remains connected, a dielectric slab of dielectric constant K is inserted between the plates. What happens to the electric field E and stored energy U?

options.text: A) E decreases by 1/K, U increases by K
options.trap: Trap: Assumed capacitor was disconnected from battery!

options.text: B) E remains unchanged, U increases by a factor of K
options.trap: Correct: Battery connected means potential V is constant => E = V/d is unchanged. Capacitance C' = K·C => U' = (1/2) C' V² = K · U.

options.text: C) Both E and U decrease by 1/K
options.trap: Trap: Confused with isolated capacitor.

options.text: D) Both E and U remain unchanged
options.trap: Trap: Ignores capacitance change.

questions.trap_warning: CRITICAL NEET TRAP: Check if battery is 'CONNECTED' (V = constant) vs 'DISCONNECTED' (Q = constant)!
questions.explanation: Since the battery remains connected, the potential difference V remains strictly constant across the plates. Therefore, electric field E = V/d remains constant. Capacitance increases from C to K·C, so energy U = (1/2) C V² increases by a factor of K.

questions.source: NEET PYQ 2024 / NCERT Exemplar Class 12 Ch 3
questions.question: A uniform wire of resistance R is stretched uniformly such that its length increases by 10%. What is the percentage increase in its resistance?

options.trap: Trap: Forgot that volume conservation causes cross-sectional area to decrease as length increases!
Correct: Volume V = A·L is constant => A ∝ 1/L => R ∝ L². If L' = 1.1 L, R' = (1.1)² R = 1.21 R => 21% increase.
Trap: Used small approximation formula ΔR/R ≈ 2 ΔL/L, but 10% is not infinitesimally small!
Trap: Distractor.

questions.trap_warning: Stretching a wire conserves volume, so R ∝ L². For finite changes (10%), calculate (1.1)² = 1.21 => 21%, NOT 20%!
questions.explanation: Resistance R = ρ L / A. When stretched, Volume = A · L = constant => A = Vol / L. R = ρ L² / Vol ∝ L². New length L' = 1.10 L. New resistance R' = (1.10)² R = 1.21 R. Percentage increase = ((1.21 - 1) / 1) * 100 = 21%.

questions.source: NEET PYQ 2023 / NCERT Exemplar Class 12 Ch 4
questions.question: A charged particle moves with velocity v in a uniform magnetic field B. What is the power delivered by the magnetic force to the charged particle?

options.text: A) q (v · B)
options.trap: Trap: Incorrect scalar product.

options.text: B) Zero
options.trap: Correct: Magnetic force F = q(v × B) is always perpendicular to velocity v => Power P = F · v = 0.

options.text: C) q v B
options.trap: Trap: Assumed collinear force and velocity.

options.text: D) (1/2) q v² B
options.trap: Trap: Energy confusion.

questions.trap_warning: Magnetic Lorentz force can NEVER do work on a free charge. Kinetic energy and speed remain strictly invariant!
questions.explanation: The magnetic force Fm = q (v × B) is inherently perpendicular to the velocity vector v at every instant. Instantaneous power P = Fm · v = q (v × B) · v = 0. Therefore, a magnetic field changes the trajectory direction but does zero work.

questions.source: NEET PYQ 2024 / NCERT Exemplar Class 12 Ch 9
questions.question: A convex lens of focal length f and refractive index μ_lens = 1.5 is immersed in water of refractive index μ_water = 1.33. Its new focal length f' in water is:

options.text: A) f' = f
options.trap: Trap: Assumed focal length is an intrinsic property of the glass lens only.

options.text: B) f' ≈ 4 f
options.trap: Correct: By Lens Maker's Formula 1/f = (μ_rel - 1)(1/R1 - 1/R2). In water, (1.5/1.33 - 1) = 0.125 = (1/4) of (1.5 - 1) => f' = 4f.
Trap: Inverted ratio.

options.text: D) It becomes a concave lens
options.trap: Trap: Occurs only if medium index exceeds lens index (μ_med > μ_lens).

questions.trap_warning: Focal length is determined by RELATIVE refractive index (μ_lens / μ_medium). In water, a glass lens's focal length quadruples (4x)!
questions.explanation: Lens Maker's equation: 1/f_air = (1.5 - 1) K = 0.5 K. In water: 1/f_water = (1.5/1.33 - 1) K = (0.128) K. Ratio f_water / f_air = 0.5 / 0.128 ≈ 3.93 ≈ 4 f.

questions.source: NEET PYQ 2023 / NCERT Exemplar Class 12 Ch 11
questions.question: In a photoelectric experiment, if the frequency of incident light is doubled while keeping its intensity constant, what happens to the saturation photoelectric current and stopping potential?

options.text: A) Saturation current doubles, stopping potential doubles
options.trap: Trap: Saturation current depends on photon arrival RATE, not photon frequency!

options.text: B) Saturation current is halved, stopping potential more than doubles
options.trap: Correct: Constant Intensity I = N·hν => if ν doubles, photon flux N is halved (current halves). Stopping potential eV0 = hν - Φ => V0 more than doubles.

options.text: C) Saturation current remains constant, stopping potential doubles
options.trap: Trap: Overlooked that constant intensity at higher frequency means FEWER photons per second.

options.text: D) Both remain unchanged
options.trap: Trap: Distractor.

questions.trap_warning: MASTERCLASS TRAP: Intensity = (Number of Photons × Energy per Photon). At constant intensity, doubling frequency cuts photon count in half!
questions.explanation: Intensity I = N · hν / (A · t). When ν is doubled at constant I, the number of incident photons per second N must halve! Since each photon ejects at most one electron, saturation current halves. For stopping potential: e V0 = hν - Φ => e V0' = 2hν - Φ = 2(hν - Φ) + Φ > 2 e V0, so stopping potential more than doubles.

questions.question: In [Physics and Measurement] Concept 2, considering the relationship expressed by its governing law, which statement correctly identifies the boundary conditions or physical significance?

options.text: A) The relation holds strictly within its declared frame and sign convention:
options.trap: Correct: Satisfies physical limits and vector rules.

options.text: B) Scalar equations apply uniformly without regard to direction or coordinate axes orientation.
options.trap: Trap: Neglects vector resolution and directional signs.

options.text: C) Gravitational and inertial parameters can be assumed constant in arbitrary relativistic frames.
options.trap: Trap: Fails outside standard Newtonian bounds.

options.text: D) Energy conservation guarantees that instantaneous power remains constant.
options.trap: Trap: Confuses conservation of total energy with rate of work done.

questions.question: In Time of Flight, considering the relationship expressed by T = (2 · v₀ · sin(θ)) / g, which statement correctly identifies the boundary conditions or physical significance?

options.trap: Trap: Neglects vector resolution and directional signs.

options.text: C) Gravitational and inertial parameters can be assumed constant in arbitrary relativistic frames.

questions.trap_warning: Question specifies angle with vertical axis instead of horizontal (swapping sin with cos).
questions.explanation: Official Rule: Time of flight is determined purely by the vertical component of initial velocity. HCV Ch 3: The horizontal velocity component vx has zero acceleration and does not affect the time spent in the air.
